The change adds a PR-body format check for Launchpad references, but as written it enforces the opposite of the format it claims to introduce.

Blocking issues:
1. `.github/workflows/ci.yaml:172` requires a digit immediately after `LP:` and therefore rejects `Fixes LP: #1234` — the documented Launchpad syntax (`LP: #<LP-Bug-Number>`) and the exact form named in the PR description — while accepting legacy `Fixes LP:1234`. Valid PRs would fail CI and legacy ones would pass.
2. `.github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml:24` is not updated and keeps the digit-only pattern. Once people start writing `LP: #1234`, the post-merge job logs "No Launchpad bug ID found" and silently stops moving bugs to Fix Committed — the exact silent failure this change is meant to prevent. The two copies of the keyword/format logic must be updated together (better: extracted into one tested script).
3. The PR description lists work that is not in this diff: no code writes a comment with the PR/commit link to the LP bug (`utilities/mark_lp_bug_fix_committed.py` only sets the task status), and the repository convention in `AGENTS.md` (lines 99, 131, 154) still documents `Resolves LP:2066936`, so the newly enforced format is undocumented and contradicts the guidelines developers are told to follow.
4. No test exists for the accept/reject matrix. Given the regex duplication and the `#` bug above, a small script under `utilities/` with unit tests (e.g. `LP: 123`, `LP: #123`, `LP:# 123`, `HELP: 123`, multiline) would have caught both.

Non-issues: passing the body through an `env:` variable and quoting it is correct — no comment/body injection into the shell. The step being inside the `pull_request`-only job is fine.

Verification performed: matched the new patterns against the Launchpad comment-syntax docs (multi-bug form is `LP: #<number>`, whitespace variable) and inspected `lp-bug-update.yaml` and `mark_lp_bug_fix_committed.py` in the working tree.

.github/workflows/ci.yaml.166: Step name says "Verify Launchpad bug reference", but it only validates when a closing keyword is present: a `fix` PR with no `Fixes/Closes/Resolves` line passes, even though `AGENTS.md` makes a ticket reference mandatory for `fix` commits. It also checks the PR description, whereas `lp-bug-update.yaml` parses `github.event.commits[].message` — with merge-commit merges the body never reaches the commit, so the rule is enforced on an artifact the consumer does not read. Either validate the text that becomes the commit message or document the squash assumption.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.170: Only the keywords are copied here; the regex is a duplicate of `.github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml:24`, which this change does not touch. The two definitions already disagree (that one accepts no `#`, this one is described as accepting `#`), so they will keep drifting and a green PR check will not imply the post-merge LP update works. Move the keyword set plus the reference pattern into one script under `utilities/` consumed by both workflows, and cover it with tests.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.171: Two problems with the outer probe. (a) There is no left word boundary on `LP:`, so `Fixes HELP: 42` matches here and the inner pattern also matches, accepting an unrelated string as a bug reference (the extractor would then operate on bug 42). Use `\bLP:`. (b) Both greps are line-oriented, so `Fixes LP:` followed by `#1234` on the next line — which Launchpad itself parses — is treated as "keyword present, reference invalid". Normalize the body first if multi-line references are meant to be legal. Also, `.*` allows arbitrary text between the keyword and the reference, so one valid reference anywhere on the line satisfies the check even when the intended one is malformed.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.172: This pattern rejects the format the change is meant to enforce. `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` requires a digit immediately after the colon and whitespace, so `Fixes LP: #1234` fails while legacy `Fixes LP:1234` passes — inverted relative to the PR description and to the Launchpad docs (`LP: #<LP-Bug-Number>`, whitespace variable). Use `\bLP:\s*#?\s*\K[0-9]+` (or require the `#` if the legacy form is being retired) and apply the identical pattern in `lp-bug-update.yaml`; otherwise standard-format commits will make the post-merge workflow log "No Launchpad bug ID found" and silently skip the bug update.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.174: The error message advertises `LP:<number>`, i.e. the legacy form this change says it deprecates, so anyone following the message will still produce the wrong syntax. Print the accepted form (e.g. `LP: #<number>`) and, for debuggability, echo the offending line.
